# pipeline-rs

Rust port of `src/pipeline.ts`, bridged with napi-rs. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `normalize` (`src/pipeline.ts:7`)
- `countWords` (`src/pipeline.ts:14`)
- `upper` (`src/pipeline.ts:19`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the TS code does
mojo-anything build .    # build the napi-rs module
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against Rust
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # fmt, clippy, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

# text-rs

Rust port of `src/main/java/com/example/text/`, bridged with a JSON dispatcher. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `gcd` (`src/main/java/com/example/text/Nums.java:7`)
- `mean` (`src/main/java/com/example/text/Nums.java:18`)
- `pages` (`src/main/java/com/example/text/Nums.java:29`)
- `slugify` (`src/main/java/com/example/text/Strings.java:14`)

- `frequencies` (`src/main/java/com/example/text/Strings.java:48`)
- `parsePort` (`src/main/java/com/example/text/Strings.java:57`)
- `hash` (`src/main/java/com/example/text/Strings.java:66`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the TS code does
mojo-anything build .    # build the a JSON dispatcher module

#!/bin/sh
# The batches against the original Java methods. The wrapper classes have the original names, so
# each side runs in its own JVM; equal digests mean equal results and errors.
# Run after `mojo-anything build ..`: sh run.sh
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
out=$(mktemp -d)
javac -d "$out/orig" $(find ../../../../tests/fixtures/java/src/main -name '*.java') Common.java Orig.java
javac -d "$out/rust" $(find ../java -name '*.java') Common.java Rust.java
java -cp "$out/orig" Orig
java -Djava.library.path=../target/release -cp "$out/rust" Rust

set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

javac -d "$out/orig" $(find ../../../../tests/fixtures/java/src/main -name '*.java') Common.java Orig.java
javac -d "$out/rust" $(find ../java -name '*.java') Common.java Rust.java
java -cp "$out/orig" Orig
java -Djava.library.path=../target/release -cp "$out/rust" Rust

import sys, time

# `SlugifyBatch`, `PageCountBatch` and `WordCountBatch` against the Ruby originals: same results,
# same errors, and the time for 20,000 slugs. Run after `mojo-anything build .`: ruby bench_batch.rb
crate = __dir__
fixture = File.expand_path("../../../tests/fixtures/ruby", __dir__)
require File.join(fixture, "lib/textkit")
texts = (0...20_000).map { |i| "Hello, Wörld #{i} -- Ünïcode Title_#{i % 7}! ΣΊΣΥΦΟΣ" }
want = texts.map { |t| Textkit::Words.slugify(t) }
want2 = texts.map { |t| Textkit::Words.slugify(t, "_", max: 12) }
totals = (0...20_000).to_a
want_pages = totals.map { |t| Textkit::Nums.page_count(t, 7) }
want_counts = texts.first(500).map { |t| Textkit::Words.word_count(t) }
t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC); 5.times { texts.map { |x| Textkit::Words.slugify(x) } }; ruby_ms = (Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t) * 200
require File.join(crate, "ruby/textkit_rs")
b = Textkit::Words::SlugifyBatch.new(texts)
raise "slug" unless b.run == want
raise "slug2" unless b.run("_", max: 12) == want2
p = Textkit::Nums::PageCountBatch.new(totals)
raise "pages" unless p.run(7) == want_pages
order = p.rank(3, min: 2000)
expect = totals.select { |x| x.fdiv(1) >= 0 && (Textkit::Nums.page_count(x, 3) rescue -1) >= 2000 }
raise "rank" unless order.map { |i| totals[i] } == expect.sort_by.with_index { |x, i| [-Textkit::Nums.page_count(x, 3), i] }
raise "counts" unless Textkit::Words::WordCountBatch.new(texts.first(500)).run == want_counts
begin; p.run(0); puts "no error?"; rescue => e; puts "batch raises #{e.class}: #{e.message}"; end
t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC); 5.times { b.run }; rust_ms = (Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t) * 200
puts format("slugify x20000: Ruby %.1f ms, batch %.1f ms: %.1fx", ruby_ms, rust_ms, ruby_ms / rust_ms)

# The Rust port of `lib/textkit/`, generated by mojo-anything: the same module functions, each
# calling the Rust extension `textkit_rs_native`. Load it in place of the original files.
# Regenerate with `mojo-anything refresh`.

require_relative "textkit_rs_native"

module Textkit
  module Nums
    def self.page_count(total, per_page = 10)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.page_count(total, per_page)
    end

    def self.mean(values)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.mean(values)
    end

    def self.clamp(value, low, high)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.clamp(value, low, high)
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Words
    def self.slugify(text, sep = "-", max: nil)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.slugify(text, sep, max)
    end

    def self.word_count(text)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.word_count(text)
    end

    def self.titleize(text)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.titleize(text)
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Words
    # `slugify` over many `text` values kept in Rust: built once, then each `run` maps them all
    # in one call, on all cores.
    class SlugifyBatch
      def initialize(texts)
        @native = MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs::SlugifyBatch.new(texts.to_a)
      end

      # The result for every item, in order.
      def run(sep = "-", max: nil)
        @native.run(sep, max)
      end
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Nums
    # `page_count` over many `total` values kept in Rust: built once, then each `run` maps them all
    # in one call, on all cores.
    class PageCountBatch
      def initialize(totals)
        @native = MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs::PageCountBatch.new(totals.to_a)
      end

      # The result for every item, in order.
      def run(per_page = 10)
        @native.run(per_page)
      end

      # Indexes of the items whose result is at least `min`, highest result first.
      def rank(per_page = 10, min: 0)
        @native.rank(per_page, min)
      end
    end
  end
end

    class WordCountBatch

      end

      def run()

# The Rust port of `lib/textkit/`, generated by mojo-anything: the same module functions, each
# calling the Rust library through Fiddle. Load it in place of the original files.
# Regenerate with `mojo-anything refresh`.

require "fiddle"
require "json"

module MojoAnythingCodec
  module_function

  def enc(v)
    case v
    when Float
      return { "$num" => "NaN" } if v.nan?
      return { "$num" => v.positive? ? "Infinity" : "-Infinity" } if v.infinite?
      return { "$num" => "-0" } if v.zero? && (1.0 / v).negative?

      v
    when Integer, String, true, false, nil then v
    when Symbol then { "$sym" => v.to_s }
    when Array then v.map { |x| enc(x) }
    when Hash
      if v.keys.all? { |k| k.is_a?(String) }
        v.transform_values { |x| enc(x) }
      else
        { "$hash" => v.map { |k, x| [enc(k), enc(x)] } }
      end
    else
      { "$object" => v.class.name, "value" => v.respond_to?(:to_h) ? enc(v.to_h) : v.inspect }
    end
  end

  def dec(v)
    case v
    when Array then v.map { |x| dec(x) }
    when Hash
      if v.size == 1 && v.key?("$num")
        { "NaN" => Float::NAN, "Infinity" => Float::INFINITY, "-Infinity" => -Float::INFINITY, "-0" => -0.0 }.fetch(v["$num"])
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$undefined")
        nil
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$sym")
        v["$sym"].to_sym
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$hash")
        v["$hash"].to_h { |k, x| [dec(k), dec(x)] }
      else
        v.transform_values { |x| dec(x) }
      end
    else v
    end
  end
end

# textkit-rs

Rust port of `lib/textkit/`, bridged with a JSON dispatcher. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `page_count` (`lib/textkit/nums.rb:9`)
- `mean` (`lib/textkit/nums.rb:17`)
- `clamp` (`lib/textkit/nums.rb:27`)
- `slugify` (`lib/textkit/words.rb:9`)
- `word_count` (`lib/textkit/words.rb:16`)
- `titleize` (`lib/textkit/words.rb:22`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the TS code does
mojo-anything build .    # build the a JSON dispatcher module
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against Rust
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches

# `SlugifyBatch`, `PageCountBatch` and `WordCountBatch` against the Ruby originals: same results,
# same errors, and the time for 20,000 slugs. Run after `mojo-anything build .`: ruby bench_batch.rb
crate = __dir__
fixture = File.expand_path("../../../tests/fixtures/ruby", __dir__)
require File.join(fixture, "lib/textkit")
texts = (0...20_000).map { |i| "Hello, Wörld #{i} -- Ünïcode Title_#{i % 7}! ΣΊΣΥΦΟΣ" }
want = texts.map { |t| Textkit::Words.slugify(t) }
want2 = texts.map { |t| Textkit::Words.slugify(t, "_", max: 12) }
totals = (0...20_000).to_a
want_pages = totals.map { |t| Textkit::Nums.page_count(t, 7) }
want_counts = texts.first(500).map { |t| Textkit::Words.word_count(t) }
t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC); 5.times { texts.map { |x| Textkit::Words.slugify(x) } }; ruby_ms = (Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t) * 200
require File.join(crate, "ruby/textkit_rs")
b = Textkit::Words::SlugifyBatch.new(texts)
raise "slug" unless b.run == want
raise "slug2" unless b.run("_", max: 12) == want2
p = Textkit::Nums::PageCountBatch.new(totals)
raise "pages" unless p.run(7) == want_pages
order = p.rank(3, min: 2000)
expect = totals.select { |x| x.fdiv(1) >= 0 && (Textkit::Nums.page_count(x, 3) rescue -1) >= 2000 }
raise "rank" unless order.map { |i| totals[i] } == expect.sort_by.with_index { |x, i| [-Textkit::Nums.page_count(x, 3), i] }
raise "counts" unless Textkit::Words::WordCountBatch.new(texts.first(500)).run == want_counts
begin; p.run(0); puts "no error?"; rescue => e; puts "batch raises #{e.class}: #{e.message}"; end
t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC); 5.times { b.run }; rust_ms = (Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t) * 200
puts format("slugify x20000: Ruby %.1f ms, batch %.1f ms: %.1fx", ruby_ms, rust_ms, ruby_ms / rust_ms)

    case v

      return { "$num" => v.positive? ? "Infinity" : "-Infinity" } if v.infinite?
      return { "$num" => "-0" } if v.zero? && (1.0 / v).negative?

        v["$hash"].to_h { |k, x| [dec(k), dec(x)] }

# The Rust port of `lib/textkit/`, generated by mojo-anything: the same module functions, each
# calling the Rust extension `textkit_rs_native`. Load it in place of the original files.
# Regenerate with `mojo-anything refresh`.

require_relative "textkit_rs_native"

module Textkit
  module Nums
    def self.page_count(total, per_page = 10)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.page_count(total, per_page)
    end

      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.mean(values)
    end

    def self.clamp(value, low, high)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.clamp(value, low, high)
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Words
    def self.slugify(text, sep = "-", max: nil)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.slugify(text, sep, max)
    end

    def self.word_count(text)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.word_count(text)
    end

    def self.titleize(text)

    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Words
    # `slugify` over many `text` values kept in Rust: built once, then each `run` maps them all
    # in one call, on all cores.
    class SlugifyBatch
      def initialize(texts)
        @native = MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs::SlugifyBatch.new(texts.to_a)
      end

      # The result for every item, in order.
      def run(sep = "-", max: nil)
        @native.run(sep, max)
      end
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Nums
    # `page_count` over many `total` values kept in Rust: built once, then each `run` maps them all
    # in one call, on all cores.
    class PageCountBatch
      def initialize(totals)
        @native = MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs::PageCountBatch.new(totals.to_a)
      end

      # The result for every item, in order.
      def run(per_page = 10)
        @native.run(per_page)
      end

      def rank(per_page = 10, min: 0)

    end
  end

# The Rust port of `lib/textkit/`, generated by mojo-anything: the same module functions, each
# calling the Rust library through Fiddle. Load it in place of the original files.
# Regenerate with `mojo-anything refresh`.

require "fiddle"
require "json"

module MojoAnythingCodec
  module_function

  def enc(v)
    case v
    when Float
      return { "$num" => "NaN" } if v.nan?
      return { "$num" => v.positive? ? "Infinity" : "-Infinity" } if v.infinite?
      return { "$num" => "-0" } if v.zero? && (1.0 / v).negative?

      v
    when Integer, String, true, false, nil then v
    when Symbol then { "$sym" => v.to_s }
    when Array then v.map { |x| enc(x) }
    when Hash
      if v.keys.all? { |k| k.is_a?(String) }
        v.transform_values { |x| enc(x) }
      else
        { "$hash" => v.map { |k, x| [enc(k), enc(x)] } }
      end
    else
      { "$object" => v.class.name, "value" => v.respond_to?(:to_h) ? enc(v.to_h) : v.inspect }
    end
  end

  def dec(v)
    case v
    when Array then v.map { |x| dec(x) }
    when Hash
      if v.size == 1 && v.key?("$num")
        { "NaN" => Float::NAN, "Infinity" => Float::INFINITY, "-Infinity" => -Float::INFINITY, "-0" => -0.0 }.fetch(v["$num"])
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$undefined")
        nil
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$sym")
        v["$sym"].to_sym
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$hash")
        v["$hash"].to_h { |k, x| [dec(k), dec(x)] }
      else
        v.transform_values { |x| dec(x) }
      end
    else v
    end
  end
end

module MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs
  names = %w[libtextkit_rs.so libtextkit_rs.dylib textkit_rs.dll]
  path = names.map { |n| File.expand_path("../target/release/#{n}", __dir__) }.find { |p| File.exist?(p) }
  raise LoadError, "build the Rust library first (mojo-anything build)" unless path

  LIB = Fiddle.dlopen(path)
  CALL = Fiddle::Function.new(LIB["mojo_anything_call"], [Fiddle::TYPE_VOIDP, Fiddle::TYPE_VOIDP], Fiddle::TYPE_VOIDP)
  FREE = Fiddle::Function.new(LIB["mojo_anything_free"], [Fiddle::TYPE_VOIDP], Fiddle::TYPE_VOID)

  def self.call(name, args)
    answer_ptr = CALL.call(Fiddle::Pointer["#{name}\0"], Fiddle::Pointer["#{JSON.generate(MojoAnythingCodec.enc(args))}\0"])
    text = answer_ptr.to_s.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
    FREE.call(answer_ptr)
    answer = JSON.parse(text)
    return MojoAnythingCodec.dec(answer["ok"]) if answer.key?("ok")

    message = answer["error"] || "Rust panic: #{answer["panic"]}"
    type, rest = message.split(": ", 2)
    klass = rest && type.match?(/\A[A-Z]\w*(::[A-Z]\w*)*\z/) ? (Object.const_get(type) rescue nil) : nil
    raise klass, rest if klass.is_a?(Class) && klass <= Exception

    raise message
  end
end

    end
  end

# textkit-rs

Rust port of `lib/textkit/`, bridged with a JSON dispatcher. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `page_count` (`lib/textkit/nums.rb:9`)
- `mean` (`lib/textkit/nums.rb:17`)
- `clamp` (`lib/textkit/nums.rb:27`)
- `slugify` (`lib/textkit/words.rb:9`)
- `word_count` (`lib/textkit/words.rb:16`)
- `titleize` (`lib/textkit/words.rb:22`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the TS code does
mojo-anything build .    # build the a JSON dispatcher module
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against Rust
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # fmt, clippy, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

# The Rust port of `lib/textkit/`, generated by mojo-anything: the same module functions, each
# calling the Rust extension `textkit_rs_native`. Load it in place of the original files.
# Regenerate with `mojo-anything refresh`.

require_relative "textkit_rs_native"

module Textkit
  module Nums
    def self.page_count(total, per_page = 10)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.page_count(total, per_page)
    end

    def self.mean(values)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.mean(values)
    end

    def self.clamp(value, low, high)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.clamp(value, low, high)
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Words
    def self.slugify(text, sep = "-", max: nil)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.slugify(text, sep, max)
    end

    def self.word_count(text)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.word_count(text)
    end

    def self.titleize(text)
      MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.titleize(text)
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Words
    # `slugify` over many `text` values kept in Rust: built once, then each `run` maps them all
    # in one call, on all cores.
    class SlugifyBatch
      def initialize(texts)
        @native = MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs::SlugifyBatch.new(texts.to_a)
      end

      # The result for every item, in order.
      def run(sep = "-", max: nil)
        @native.run(sep, max)
      end
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Nums
    # `page_count` over many `total` values kept in Rust: built once, then each `run` maps them all
    # in one call, on all cores.
    class PageCountBatch
      def initialize(totals)
        @native = MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs::PageCountBatch.new(totals.to_a)
      end

      # The result for every item, in order.
      def run(per_page = 10)
        @native.run(per_page)
      end

      # Indexes of the items whose result is at least `min`, highest result first.
      def rank(per_page = 10, min: 0)
        @native.rank(per_page, min)
      end
    end
  end
end

module Textkit
  module Words
    # `word_count` over many `text` values kept in Rust: built once, then each `run` maps them all
    # in one call, on all cores.
    class WordCountBatch
      def initialize(texts)
        @native = MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs::WordCountBatch.new(texts.to_a)
      end

      # The result for every item, in order.
      def run()
        @native.run()
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# The Rust port of `lib/textkit/`, generated by mojo-anything: the same module functions, each
# calling the Rust library through Fiddle. Load it in place of the original files.
# Regenerate with `mojo-anything refresh`.

require "fiddle"
require "json"

module MojoAnythingCodec
  module_function

  def enc(v)
    case v
    when Float
      return { "$num" => "NaN" } if v.nan?
      return { "$num" => v.positive? ? "Infinity" : "-Infinity" } if v.infinite?
      return { "$num" => "-0" } if v.zero? && (1.0 / v).negative?

      v
    when Integer, String, true, false, nil then v
    when Symbol then { "$sym" => v.to_s }
    when Array then v.map { |x| enc(x) }
    when Hash
      if v.keys.all? { |k| k.is_a?(String) }
        v.transform_values { |x| enc(x) }
      else
        { "$hash" => v.map { |k, x| [enc(k), enc(x)] } }
      end
    else
      { "$object" => v.class.name, "value" => v.respond_to?(:to_h) ? enc(v.to_h) : v.inspect }
    end
  end

  def dec(v)
    case v
    when Array then v.map { |x| dec(x) }
    when Hash
      if v.size == 1 && v.key?("$num")
        { "NaN" => Float::NAN, "Infinity" => Float::INFINITY, "-Infinity" => -Float::INFINITY, "-0" => -0.0 }.fetch(v["$num"])
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$undefined")
        nil
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$sym")
        v["$sym"].to_sym
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$hash")
        v["$hash"].to_h { |k, x| [dec(k), dec(x)] }
      else
        v.transform_values { |x| dec(x) }
      end
    else v
    end
  end
end

module MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs
  names = %w[libtextkit_rs.so libtextkit_rs.dylib textkit_rs.dll]
  path = names.map { |n| File.expand_path("../target/release/#{n}", __dir__) }.find { |p| File.exist?(p) }
  raise LoadError, "build the Rust library first (mojo-anything build)" unless path

  LIB = Fiddle.dlopen(path)
  CALL = Fiddle::Function.new(LIB["mojo_anything_call"], [Fiddle::TYPE_VOIDP, Fiddle::TYPE_VOIDP], Fiddle::TYPE_VOIDP)
  FREE = Fiddle::Function.new(LIB["mojo_anything_free"], [Fiddle::TYPE_VOIDP], Fiddle::TYPE_VOID)

  def self.call(name, args)
    answer_ptr = CALL.call(Fiddle::Pointer["#{name}\0"], Fiddle::Pointer["#{JSON.generate(MojoAnythingCodec.enc(args))}\0"])
    text = answer_ptr.to_s.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
    FREE.call(answer_ptr)
    answer = JSON.parse(text)
    return MojoAnythingCodec.dec(answer["ok"]) if answer.key?("ok")

    message = answer["error"] || "Rust panic: #{answer["panic"]}"
    type, rest = message.split(": ", 2)
    klass = rest && type.match?(/\A[A-Z]\w*(::[A-Z]\w*)*\z/) ? (Object.const_get(type) rescue nil) : nil
    raise klass, rest if klass.is_a?(Class) && klass <= Exception

    raise message
  end
end

module MojoAnythingShadow
  MODE = ENV.fetch("MOJO_ANYTHING_MODE", "shadow")
  @calls = 0
  @mismatches = 0

  class << self
    attr_reader :calls, :mismatches

    def compare(name, expected, actual)
      @calls += 1
      return if JSON.generate(MojoAnythingCodec.enc(expected)) == JSON.generate(MojoAnythingCodec.enc(actual))

      @mismatches += 1
      warn "[mojo-anything] mismatch in #{name}: expected #{expected.inspect}, got #{actual.inspect}" if @mismatches <= 10
    end
  end
end

Textkit::Nums.singleton_class.prepend(Module.new do
               def page_count(total, per_page = 10)
                 return MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.call("page_count", [total, per_page]) if MojoAnythingShadow::MODE == "new"

                 expected = super
                 unless MojoAnythingShadow::MODE == "old"
                   actual = begin
        MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.call("page_count", [total, per_page])
                   rescue StandardError => e
        e
      end
                   MojoAnythingShadow.compare("Textkit::Nums.page_count", expected, actual)
    end
                 expected
  end
end)

Textkit::Nums.singleton_class.prepend(Module.new do
               def mean(values)
                 return MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.call("mean", [values]) if MojoAnythingShadow::MODE == "new"

                 expected = super
                 unless MojoAnythingShadow::MODE == "old"
                   actual = begin
        MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.call("mean", [values])
                   rescue StandardError => e
        e
      end
                   MojoAnythingShadow.compare("Textkit::Nums.mean", expected, actual)
    end
                 expected
  end
end)

Textkit::Nums.singleton_class.prepend(Module.new do
               def clamp(value, low, high)
                 return MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.call("clamp", [value, low, high]) if MojoAnythingShadow::MODE == "new"

    end
                 expected

end)

Textkit::Words.singleton_class.prepend(Module.new do
               def slugify(text, sep = "-", max: nil)
                 return MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.call("slugify", [text, sep, max]) if MojoAnythingShadow::MODE == "new"

                 expected = super
                 unless MojoAnythingShadow::MODE == "old"

                   rescue StandardError => e

                   MojoAnythingShadow.compare("Textkit::Words.slugify", expected, actual)

                 expected

end)

                 return MojoAnythingNativeTextkitRs.call("word_count", [text]) if MojoAnythingShadow::MODE == "new"

# facade-mojo

Mojo port of `src/facade.c`, bridged with the C ABI. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `parse_long` (`src/facade.c:6`)
- `parse_int` (`src/facade.c:7`)
- `parse_double` (`src/facade.c:8`)
- `span` (`src/facade.c:9`)
- `compare` (`src/facade.c:10`)
- `is_alpha` (`src/facade.c:14`)
- `is_space` (`src/facade.c:15`)
- `is_punct` (`src/facade.c:16`)
- `to_upper` (`src/facade.c:17`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does
mojo-anything build .    # build the C ABI
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against the port
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # format, lint, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

## Result

`cases.jsonl` was recorded on 2026-11-21 (glibc 2.39, Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL) from
`original/facade.c` with `inputs.jsonl`: 2,488 cases, 12 of them crashes. The Mojo port
matches 2,488/2,488 of them, and 1,859/1,859 of the cases the Rust port was recorded with
(2026-11-16); `gate` passes. To record again, put `original/facade.c` at `src/facade.c` of a
folder, point `root` in `mojo-anything.json` at it, and run
`mojo-anything record . --inputs inputs.jsonl` here.

files.README.md:
# facade-mojo

Mojo port of `src/facade.c`, bridged with the C ABI. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `parse_long` (`src/facade.c:6`)
- `parse_int` (`src/facade.c:7`)
- `parse_double` (`src/facade.c:8`)
- `span` (`src/facade.c:9`)
- `compare` (`src/facade.c:10`)
- `is_alpha` (`src/facade.c:14`)
- `is_space` (`src/facade.c:15`)
- `is_punct` (`src/facade.c:16`)
- `to_upper` (`src/facade.c:17`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does
mojo-anything build .    # build the C ABI
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against the port
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # format, lint, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

## Result

`cases.jsonl` was recorded on 2026-11-21 (glibc 2.39, Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL) from
`original/facade.c` with `inputs.jsonl`: 2,488 cases, 12 of them crashes. The Mojo port
matches 2,488/2,488 of them, and 1,859/1,859 of the cases the Rust port was recorded with
(2026-11-16); `gate` passes. To record again, put `original/facade.c` at `src/facade.c` of a
folder, point `root` in `mojo-anything.json` at it, and run
`mojo-anything record . --inputs inputs.jsonl` here.

files.README.md:
# ffmpeg-mojo

FFmpeg `libavutil` (tag `n7.1`, commit `b08d796`) ported to Mojo with mojo-anything, starting
with `rational.c`. Each unit is proven against recordings of the real ffmpeg functions and passes
`mojo-anything gate`. The Rust ports of the same units, made before mojo-anything targeted Mojo,
are in [`../ffmpeg-rs`](../ffmpeg-rs) and stay there as the reference.

## License

libavutil is LGPL-2.1-or-later. The Mojo in this folder ports it, so it is LGPL-2.1-or-later too
(the license text is [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)); each `port.mojo` names the file it ports and that
file's copyright holders. No ffmpeg source, test or recorded case is copied here: the scripts
clone ffmpeg and regenerate them.

## What is here

| Unit | Ports | Exports (C ABI, original signatures) | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `rational-mojo` | `rational.c` | `av_reduce`, `av_mul_q`, `av_div_q`, `av_add_q`, `av_sub_q`, `av_d2q`, `av_nearer_q`, `av_q2intfloat` | 46,764 |

Every recorded call is matched by the Mojo (2026-11-21, Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL, Mojo 1.2.0, gcc
13). The inputs are those of `../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/inputs.py`: the vectors of ffmpeg's own
rational tests plus seeded edge cases (`INT_MIN`/`INT_MAX` terms, zero and negative
denominators, NaN, infinities and subnormals for `av_d2q`), and mojo-anything's generated cases on
top. `av_gcd_q` and `av_find_nearest_q_idx` stay in C, as in the Rust port.

The unit builds `.mojo-anything/build/librational_mojo.so`, which exports the eight functions
under their C names with ffmpeg's signatures (`include/rational_mojo.h`): link it instead of
`rational.o` and callers do not change. `port.mojo` holds no pointers; `exports.mojo` reads and
writes them. This library needs nothing at run time (`readelf -d` lists no `NEEDED` entry), but
it carries an absolute RUNPATH into the unit's `.pixi`; a unit that uses more of the Mojo
standard library (the glibc facade does) also needs `libKGENCompilerRTShared.so` from there.
Packaging such a library to run elsewhere is not done yet.

## Found along the way

`av_q2intfloat` negates `q.num` and `q.den` with `*= -1`, which overflows for `INT_MIN`. The Rust
port matched ffmpeg's macOS build (clang 21, `-O3`), which tests the sign before the wrap and
returns `+inf` for any `x/0`. This recording compiles `rational.c` with gcc 13 at `-O1` (what
`record` uses), which wraps: `INT_MIN` stays negative through the log and the rescales, where
clang divided by 2^31. Like clang, gcc drops the sign of `x/0`. The Mojo port follows the
recording, so on the 75 inputs with an `INT_MIN` term and a nonzero denominator it gives gcc's
answer, not clang's; every other input agrees with both.

## Reproduce

Needs a C compiler, nasm, Python 3, pixi, git and make, on Linux or macOS. From the repository
root:

```sh
cargo build --release
WORK=$PWD/work demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/scripts/prepare.sh   # clone ffmpeg n7.1, build libavutil.a, assemble the tree
WORK=$PWD/work demo/real-world/ffmpeg-mojo/scripts/verify.sh  # per unit: record, build, diff, gate
```

The other nine units of `../ffmpeg-rs` (adler32, base64, mathematics, avstring, parseutils and
the four one-shot hash wrappers) are not ported to Mojo yet.
files.rational-mojo/README.md:
# rational-mojo

Mojo port of `rational.c`, bridged with the C ABI. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `av_reduce` (`rational.c:35`)
- `av_mul_q` (`rational.c:80`)
- `av_div_q` (`rational.c:88`)
- `av_add_q` (`rational.c:93`)
- `av_sub_q` (`rational.c:101`)
- `av_d2q` (`rational.c:106`)
- `av_nearer_q` (`rational.c:127`)
- `av_q2intfloat` (`rational.c:152`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does
mojo-anything build .    # build the C ABI
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against the port
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # format, lint, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

files.scripts/verify.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# For every Mojo unit: copies it next to the tree that ../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/prepare.sh
# assembles, records ffmpeg's behaviour on the inputs from ../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/inputs.py (and
# mojo-anything's generated edge cases), builds the Mojo library, replays every case and runs
# gate. Run prepare.sh first, with the same WORK. Pass unit folder names to verify only those.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)
SCRIPTS=$REPO/demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/scripts
WORK=${WORK:-$REPO/demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/work}
TREE=$WORK/tree
MA=${MA:-$REPO/target/release/mojo-anything}
[ -x "$MA" ] || cargo build --release --manifest-path "$REPO/Cargo.toml"
export CFLAGS="-I$TREE -DHAVE_AV_CONFIG_H"

units=("$@")
[ ${#units[@]} -gt 0 ] || units=(rational-mojo)
for unit_dir in "${units[@]}"; do
  unit=${unit_dir%-mojo}
  dir=$TREE/libavutil/mojo/$unit_dir
  rm -rf "$dir"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  (cd "$HERE/$unit_dir" && tar cf - --exclude .pixi --exclude .mojo-anything .) | (cd "$dir" && tar xf -)
  python3 - "$dir/mojo-anything.json" "$TREE/libavutil" <<'PY'
import json, sys
path, root = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
m = json.load(open(path))
m["root"] = root
json.dump(m, open(path, "w"), indent=2)
PY
  python3 "$SCRIPTS/inputs.py" "$unit" "$dir/inputs.jsonl"
  echo "== $unit_dir"
  "$MA" record "$dir" --inputs "$dir/inputs.jsonl" | grep Recorded | sed 's/ in .*//'
  "$MA" build "$dir" > /dev/null
  "$MA" diff "$dir" | sed -n 1p
  "$MA" gate "$dir" | tail -1
done

# ffmpeg-mojo

FFmpeg `libavutil` (tag `n7.1`, commit `b08d796`) ported to Mojo with mojo-anything, starting
with `rational.c`. Each unit is proven against recordings of the real ffmpeg functions and passes
`mojo-anything gate`. The Rust ports of the same units, made before mojo-anything targeted Mojo,
are in [`../ffmpeg-rs`](../ffmpeg-rs) and stay there as the reference.

## License

libavutil is LGPL-2.1-or-later. The Mojo in this folder ports it, so it is LGPL-2.1-or-later too
(the license text is [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)); each `port.mojo` names the file it ports and that
file's copyright holders. No ffmpeg source, test or recorded case is copied here: the scripts
clone ffmpeg and regenerate them.

## What is here

| Unit | Ports | Exports (C ABI, original signatures) | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `rational-mojo` | `rational.c` | `av_reduce`, `av_mul_q`, `av_div_q`, `av_add_q`, `av_sub_q`, `av_d2q`, `av_nearer_q`, `av_q2intfloat` | 46,764 |

Every recorded call is matched by the Mojo (2026-11-21, Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL, Mojo 1.2.0, gcc
13). The inputs are those of `../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/inputs.py`: the vectors of ffmpeg's own
rational tests plus seeded edge cases (`INT_MIN`/`INT_MAX` terms, zero and negative
denominators, NaN, infinities and subnormals for `av_d2q`), and mojo-anything's generated cases on
top. `av_gcd_q` and `av_find_nearest_q_idx` stay in C, as in the Rust port.

The unit builds `.mojo-anything/build/librational_mojo.so`, which exports the eight functions
under their C names with ffmpeg's signatures (`include/rational_mojo.h`): link it instead of
`rational.o` and callers do not change. `port.mojo` holds no pointers; `exports.mojo` reads and
writes them. This library needs nothing at run time (`readelf -d` lists no `NEEDED` entry), but
it carries an absolute RUNPATH into the unit's `.pixi`; a unit that uses more of the Mojo
standard library (the glibc facade does) also needs `libKGENCompilerRTShared.so` from there.
Packaging such a library to run elsewhere is not done yet.

## Found along the way

`av_q2intfloat` negates `q.num` and `q.den` with `*= -1`, which overflows for `INT_MIN`. The Rust
port matched ffmpeg's macOS build (clang 21, `-O3`), which tests the sign before the wrap and
returns `+inf` for any `x/0`. This recording compiles `rational.c` with gcc 13 at `-O1` (what
`record` uses), which wraps: `INT_MIN` stays negative through the log and the rescales, where
clang divided by 2^31. Like clang, gcc drops the sign of `x/0`. The Mojo port follows the
recording, so on the 75 inputs with an `INT_MIN` term and a nonzero denominator it gives gcc's
answer, not clang's; every other input agrees with both.

## Reproduce

Needs a C compiler, nasm, Python 3, pixi, git and make, on Linux or macOS. From the repository
root:

```sh
cargo build --release
WORK=$PWD/work demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/scripts/prepare.sh   # clone ffmpeg n7.1, build libavutil.a, assemble the tree
WORK=$PWD/work demo/real-world/ffmpeg-mojo/scripts/verify.sh  # per unit: record, build, diff, gate
```

The other nine units of `../ffmpeg-rs` (adler32, base64, mathematics, avstring, parseutils and
the four one-shot hash wrappers) are not ported to Mojo yet.
files.rational-mojo/README.md:
# rational-mojo

Mojo port of `rational.c`, bridged with the C ABI. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `av_reduce` (`rational.c:35`)
- `av_mul_q` (`rational.c:80`)
- `av_div_q` (`rational.c:88`)
- `av_add_q` (`rational.c:93`)
- `av_sub_q` (`rational.c:101`)
- `av_d2q` (`rational.c:106`)
- `av_nearer_q` (`rational.c:127`)
- `av_q2intfloat` (`rational.c:152`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does
mojo-anything build .    # build the C ABI
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against the port
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # format, lint, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

files.rational-mojo/pixi.toml:
# Generated by mojo-anything: the Mojo this port builds with.
[workspace]
name = "rational-mojo"
channels = ["https://conda.modular.com/max", "conda-forge"]
platforms = ["linux-64", "linux-aarch64", "osx-arm64"]

[dependencies]
mojo = "==1.2.0"
files.scripts/verify.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# For every Mojo unit: copies it next to the tree that ../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/prepare.sh
# assembles, records ffmpeg's behaviour on the inputs from ../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/inputs.py (and
# mojo-anything's generated edge cases), builds the Mojo library, replays every case and runs
# gate. Run prepare.sh first, with the same WORK. Pass unit folder names to verify only those.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)
SCRIPTS=$REPO/demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/scripts
WORK=${WORK:-$REPO/demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/work}
TREE=$WORK/tree
MA=${MA:-$REPO/target/release/mojo-anything}
[ -x "$MA" ] || cargo build --release --manifest-path "$REPO/Cargo.toml"
export CFLAGS="-I$TREE -DHAVE_AV_CONFIG_H"

units=("$@")
[ ${#units[@]} -gt 0 ] || units=(rational-mojo)
for unit_dir in "${units[@]}"; do
  unit=${unit_dir%-mojo}
  dir=$TREE/libavutil/mojo/$unit_dir
  rm -rf "$dir"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  (cd "$HERE/$unit_dir" && tar cf - --exclude .pixi --exclude .mojo-anything .) | (cd "$dir" && tar xf -)
  python3 - "$dir/mojo-anything.json" "$TREE/libavutil" <<'PY'
import json, sys
path, root = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
m = json.load(open(path))
m["root"] = root
json.dump(m, open(path, "w"), indent=2)
PY
  python3 "$SCRIPTS/inputs.py" "$unit" "$dir/inputs.jsonl"
  echo "== $unit_dir"
  "$MA" record "$dir" --inputs "$dir/inputs.jsonl" | grep Recorded | sed 's/ in .*//'
  "$MA" build "$dir" > /dev/null
  "$MA" diff "$dir" | sed -n 1p
  "$MA" gate "$dir" | tail -1
done

files.README.md:
# ffmpeg-mojo

FFmpeg `libavutil` (tag `n7.1`, commit `b08d796`) ported to Mojo with mojo-anything, starting
with `rational.c`. Each unit is proven against recordings of the real ffmpeg functions and passes
`mojo-anything gate`. The Rust ports of the same units, made before mojo-anything targeted Mojo,
are in [`../ffmpeg-rs`](../ffmpeg-rs) and stay there as the reference.

## License

libavutil is LGPL-2.1-or-later. The Mojo in this folder ports it, so it is LGPL-2.1-or-later too
(the license text is [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)); each `port.mojo` names the file it ports and that
file's copyright holders. No ffmpeg source, test or recorded case is copied here: the scripts
clone ffmpeg and regenerate them.

## What is here

| Unit | Ports | Exports (C ABI, original signatures) | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `rational-mojo` | `rational.c` | `av_reduce`, `av_mul_q`, `av_div_q`, `av_add_q`, `av_sub_q`, `av_d2q`, `av_nearer_q`, `av_q2intfloat` | 46,764 |

Every recorded call is matched by the Mojo (2026-11-21, Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL, Mojo 1.2.0, gcc
13). The inputs are those of `../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/inputs.py`: the vectors of ffmpeg's own
rational tests plus seeded edge cases (`INT_MIN`/`INT_MAX` terms, zero and negative
denominators, NaN, infinities and subnormals for `av_d2q`), and mojo-anything's generated cases on
top. `av_gcd_q` and `av_find_nearest_q_idx` stay in C, as in the Rust port.

The unit builds `.mojo-anything/build/librational_mojo.so`, which exports the eight functions
under their C names with ffmpeg's signatures (`include/rational_mojo.h`): link it instead of
`rational.o` and callers do not change. `port.mojo` holds no pointers; `exports.mojo` reads and
writes them. This library needs nothing at run time (`readelf -d` lists no `NEEDED` entry), but
it carries an absolute RUNPATH into the unit's `.pixi`; a unit that uses more of the Mojo
standard library (the glibc facade does) also needs `libKGENCompilerRTShared.so` from there.
Packaging such a library to run elsewhere is not done yet.

## Found along the way

`av_q2intfloat` negates `q.num` and `q.den` with `*= -1`, which overflows for `INT_MIN`. The Rust
port matched ffmpeg's macOS build (clang 21, `-O3`), which tests the sign before the wrap and
returns `+inf` for any `x/0`. This recording compiles `rational.c` with gcc 13 at `-O1` (what
`record` uses), which wraps: `INT_MIN` stays negative through the log and the rescales, where
clang divided by 2^31. Like clang, gcc drops the sign of `x/0`. The Mojo port follows the
recording, so on the 75 inputs with an `INT_MIN` term and a nonzero denominator it gives gcc's
answer, not clang's; every other input agrees with both.

## Reproduce

Needs a C compiler, nasm, Python 3, pixi, git and make, on Linux or macOS. From the repository
root:

```sh
cargo build --release
WORK=$PWD/work demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/scripts/prepare.sh   # clone ffmpeg n7.1, build libavutil.a, assemble the tree
WORK=$PWD/work demo/real-world/ffmpeg-mojo/scripts/verify.sh  # per unit: record, build, diff, gate
```

The other nine units of `../ffmpeg-rs` (adler32, base64, mathematics, avstring, parseutils and
the four one-shot hash wrappers) are not ported to Mojo yet.
files.rational-mojo/README.md:
# rational-mojo

Mojo port of `rational.c`, bridged with the C ABI. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `av_reduce` (`rational.c:35`)
- `av_mul_q` (`rational.c:80`)
- `av_div_q` (`rational.c:88`)
- `av_add_q` (`rational.c:93`)
- `av_sub_q` (`rational.c:101`)
- `av_d2q` (`rational.c:106`)
- `av_nearer_q` (`rational.c:127`)
- `av_q2intfloat` (`rational.c:152`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does
mojo-anything build .    # build the C ABI
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against the port
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # format, lint, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

files.scripts/verify.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# For every Mojo unit: copies it next to the tree that ../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/prepare.sh
# assembles, records ffmpeg's behaviour on the inputs from ../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/inputs.py (and
# mojo-anything's generated edge cases), builds the Mojo library, replays every case and runs
# gate. Run prepare.sh first, with the same WORK. Pass unit folder names to verify only those.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)
SCRIPTS=$REPO/demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/scripts
WORK=${WORK:-$REPO/demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/work}
TREE=$WORK/tree
MA=${MA:-$REPO/target/release/mojo-anything}
[ -x "$MA" ] || cargo build --release --manifest-path "$REPO/Cargo.toml"
export CFLAGS="-I$TREE -DHAVE_AV_CONFIG_H"

units=("$@")
[ ${#units[@]} -gt 0 ] || units=(rational-mojo)
for unit_dir in "${units[@]}"; do
  unit=${unit_dir%-mojo}
  dir=$TREE/libavutil/mojo/$unit_dir
  rm -rf "$dir"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  (cd "$HERE/$unit_dir" && tar cf - --exclude .pixi --exclude .mojo-anything .) | (cd "$dir" && tar xf -)
  python3 - "$dir/mojo-anything.json" "$TREE/libavutil" <<'PY'
import json, sys
path, root = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
m = json.load(open(path))
m["root"] = root
json.dump(m, open(path, "w"), indent=2)
PY
  python3 "$SCRIPTS/inputs.py" "$unit" "$dir/inputs.jsonl"
  echo "== $unit_dir"
  "$MA" record "$dir" --inputs "$dir/inputs.jsonl" | grep Recorded | sed 's/ in .*//'
  "$MA" build "$dir" > /dev/null
  "$MA" diff "$dir" | sed -n 1p
  "$MA" gate "$dir" | tail -1
done

# ffmpeg-mojo

FFmpeg `libavutil` (tag `n7.1`, commit `b08d796`) ported to Mojo with mojo-anything, starting
with `rational.c`. Each unit is proven against recordings of the real ffmpeg functions and passes
`mojo-anything gate`. The Rust ports of the same units, made before mojo-anything targeted Mojo,
are in [`../ffmpeg-rs`](../ffmpeg-rs) and stay there as the reference.

## License

libavutil is LGPL-2.1-or-later. The Mojo in this folder ports it, so it is LGPL-2.1-or-later too
(the license text is [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)); each `port.mojo` names the file it ports and that
file's copyright holders. No ffmpeg source, test or recorded case is copied here: the scripts
clone ffmpeg and regenerate them.

## What is here

| Unit | Ports | Exports (C ABI, original signatures) | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `rational-mojo` | `rational.c` | `av_reduce`, `av_mul_q`, `av_div_q`, `av_add_q`, `av_sub_q`, `av_d2q`, `av_nearer_q`, `av_q2intfloat` | 46,764 |

Every recorded call is matched by the Mojo (2026-11-21, Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL, Mojo 1.2.0, gcc
13). The inputs are those of `../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/inputs.py`: the vectors of ffmpeg's own
rational tests plus seeded edge cases (`INT_MIN`/`INT_MAX` terms, zero and negative
denominators, NaN, infinities and subnormals for `av_d2q`), and mojo-anything's generated cases on
top. `av_gcd_q` and `av_find_nearest_q_idx` stay in C, as in the Rust port.

The unit builds `.mojo-anything/build/librational_mojo.so`, which exports the eight functions
under their C names with ffmpeg's signatures (`include/rational_mojo.h`): link it instead of
`rational.o` and callers do not change. `port.mojo` holds no pointers; `exports.mojo` reads and
writes them. This library needs nothing at run time (`readelf -d` lists no `NEEDED` entry), but
it carries an absolute RUNPATH into the unit's `.pixi`; a unit that uses more of the Mojo
standard library (the glibc facade does) also needs `libKGENCompilerRTShared.so` from there.
Packaging such a library to run elsewhere is not done yet.

## Found along the way

`av_q2intfloat` negates `q.num` and `q.den` with `*= -1`, which overflows for `INT_MIN`. The Rust
port matched ffmpeg's macOS build (clang 21, `-O3`), which tests the sign before the wrap and
returns `+inf` for any `x/0`. This recording compiles `rational.c` with gcc 13 at `-O1` (what
`record` uses), which wraps: `INT_MIN` stays negative through the log and the rescales, where
clang divided by 2^31. Like clang, gcc drops the sign of `x/0`. The Mojo port follows the
recording, so on the 75 inputs with an `INT_MIN` term and a nonzero denominator it gives gcc's
answer, not clang's; every other input agrees with both.

## Reproduce

Needs a C compiler, nasm, Python 3, pixi, git and make, on Linux or macOS. From the repository
root:

```sh
cargo build --release
WORK=$PWD/work demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/scripts/prepare.sh   # clone ffmpeg n7.1, build libavutil.a, assemble the tree
WORK=$PWD/work demo/real-world/ffmpeg-mojo/scripts/verify.sh  # per unit: record, build, diff, gate
```

The other nine units of `../ffmpeg-rs` (adler32, base64, mathematics, avstring, parseutils and
the four one-shot hash wrappers) are not ported to Mojo yet.
files.rational-mojo/README.md:
# rational-mojo

Mojo port of `rational.c`, bridged with the C ABI. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `av_reduce` (`rational.c:35`)
- `av_mul_q` (`rational.c:80`)
- `av_div_q` (`rational.c:88`)
- `av_add_q` (`rational.c:93`)
- `av_sub_q` (`rational.c:101`)
- `av_d2q` (`rational.c:106`)
- `av_nearer_q` (`rational.c:127`)
- `av_q2intfloat` (`rational.c:152`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does
mojo-anything build .    # build the C ABI
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against the port
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # format, lint, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

files.scripts/verify.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# For every Mojo unit: copies it next to the tree that ../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/prepare.sh
# assembles, records ffmpeg's behaviour on the inputs from ../ffmpeg-rs/scripts/inputs.py (and
# mojo-anything's generated edge cases), builds the Mojo library, replays every case and runs
# gate. Run prepare.sh first, with the same WORK. Pass unit folder names to verify only those.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)
SCRIPTS=$REPO/demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/scripts
WORK=${WORK:-$REPO/demo/real-world/ffmpeg-rs/work}
TREE=$WORK/tree
MA=${MA:-$REPO/target/release/mojo-anything}
[ -x "$MA" ] || cargo build --release --manifest-path "$REPO/Cargo.toml"
export CFLAGS="-I$TREE -DHAVE_AV_CONFIG_H"

units=("$@")
[ ${#units[@]} -gt 0 ] || units=(rational-mojo)
for unit_dir in "${units[@]}"; do
  unit=${unit_dir%-mojo}
  dir=$TREE/libavutil/mojo/$unit_dir
  rm -rf "$dir"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  (cd "$HERE/$unit_dir" && tar cf - --exclude .pixi --exclude .mojo-anything .) | (cd "$dir" && tar xf -)
  python3 - "$dir/mojo-anything.json" "$TREE/libavutil" <<'PY'
import json, sys
path, root = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
m = json.load(open(path))
m["root"] = root
json.dump(m, open(path, "w"), indent=2)
PY
  python3 "$SCRIPTS/inputs.py" "$unit" "$dir/inputs.jsonl"
  echo "== $unit_dir"
  "$MA" record "$dir" --inputs "$dir/inputs.jsonl" | grep Recorded | sed 's/ in .*//'
  "$MA" build "$dir" > /dev/null
  "$MA" diff "$dir" | sed -n 1p
  "$MA" gate "$dir" | tail -1
done

# jdk-mojo

Mojo port of `src/main/java/com/example/jdk/`, bridged with Java's Foreign Function & Memory API over the JSON dispatcher. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `toRadix` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:12`)
- `parseRadix` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:16`)
- `toBinary` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:20`)
- `toHex` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:24`)
- `reverseBits` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:28`)
- `floorMod` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:32`)
- `addExact` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:36`)
- `formatDouble` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:40`)
- `urlEncode` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:44`)
- `base64` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:48`)
- `upper` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:52`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does
mojo-anything build .    # build Java's Foreign Function & Memory API over the JSON dispatcher
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against the port
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # format, lint, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

## How it was checked

OpenJDK 25.0.5.1, Mojo 1.2.0, x86-64 Linux (WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04), 2026-11-22. The original is
`original/Jdk.java`, placed at `src/main/java/com/example/jdk/` of a project with a `pom.xml`.

- `cases.jsonl`: 4,782 cases (286 throw), recorded with `inputs.jsonl` (the Rust-era inputs plus
  28 `formatDouble` values: `1.0E10`, the switch at 1e-3 and 1e7, the two-digit rule as in
  `4.9E-324` and `1.0E23`, binade edges, and values whose exact expansion ends in a 5). The port
  matches 4,782/4,782, and 4,492/4,492 on `cases.rust-era.jsonl`, the JDK 21 recording the Rust
  port passed. Every case recorded on both JDKs gives the same result; the 290 new cases come from
  the recorder's newer string and radix traps and the 28 values above. Since 2026-11-22 `diff`
  compares a thrown exception's message as well as its class: run again that way, the counts are
  unchanged (all 286 throwing cases, and the 226 of the JDK 21 recording, give the JDK's message).
  The wider check below was run before that and compared classes only.
- A wider check, not kept here (446,916 cases): 200,000 random bit patterns, 150,000 values in
  common ranges, every power of two and the first 3,999 subnormals through `formatDouble`;
  every BMP character through `parseRadix` at radix 36; and every code point, 128 at a time,
  through `upper`, `urlEncode` and `base64`. All match. It found two problems, both fixed:
  Mojo's case tables predate Unicode 16 and map the Greek letters with ypogegrammeni to title
  case where Java spells them out with capital iota (90 code points, kept in `_upper_apart`),
  and EmberJson read an escaped surrogate pair on planes 2, 4, ... 16 as the plane below (the
  Java codec now writes whole pairs as the character).
- `gate` passes: 173 lines of Mojo for 41 of Java, the size limit exactly.
- `bench` (run twice, AMD Ryzen 9 3900X, 12 cores / 24 threads, load average 1.2-1.8): every
  function is slower through the bridge, 0.03x overall. The crossing alone is about 1 µs
  (`reverseBits`: 9-10 ns in Java, 1,030 ns through Mojo); `formatDouble`, which does exact
  big-number arithmetic, takes 12-13.5 µs against 80-91 ns; `parseRadix` comes closest, 0.21x
  (1.7 µs in Java, most cases throwing, against 7.8-8.0 µs).

# jdk-mojo

Mojo port of `src/main/java/com/example/jdk/`, bridged with Java's Foreign Function & Memory API over the JSON dispatcher. Generated by mojo-anything.

## Functions

- `toRadix` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:12`)
- `parseRadix` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:16`)
- `toBinary` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:20`)
- `toHex` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:24`)
- `reverseBits` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:28`)
- `floorMod` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:32`)
- `addExact` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:36`)
- `formatDouble` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:40`)
- `urlEncode` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:44`)
- `base64` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:48`)
- `upper` (`src/main/java/com/example/jdk/Jdk.java:52`)

## Loop

```sh
mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does
mojo-anything build .    # build Java's Foreign Function & Memory API over the JSON dispatcher
mojo-anything diff .     # run the recorded cases against the port
mojo-anything shadow .   # run both in the app, log mismatches
mojo-anything gate .     # format, lint, tests, unsafe, API, diff
```

## How it was checked

OpenJDK 25.0.5.1, Mojo 1.2.0, x86-64 Linux (WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04), 2026-11-22. The original is
`original/Jdk.java`, placed at `src/main/java/com/example/jdk/` of a project with a `pom.xml`.

- `cases.jsonl`: 4,782 cases (286 throw), recorded with `inputs.jsonl` (the Rust-era inputs plus
  28 `formatDouble` values: `1.0E10`, the switch at 1e-3 and 1e7, the two-digit rule as in
  `4.9E-324` and `1.0E23`, binade edges, and values whose exact expansion ends in a 5). The port
  matches 4,782/4,782, and 4,492/4,492 on `cases.rust-era.jsonl`, the JDK 21 recording the Rust
  port passed. Every case recorded on both JDKs gives the same result; the 290 new cases come from
  the recorder's newer string and radix traps and the 28 values above. Since 2026-11-22 `diff`
  compares a thrown exception's message as well as its class: run again that way, the counts are
  unchanged (all 286 throwing cases, and the 226 of the JDK 21 recording, give the JDK's message).
  The wider check below was run before that and compared classes only.
- A wider check, not kept here (446,916 cases): 200,000 random bit patterns, 150,000 values in
  common ranges, every power of two and the first 3,999 subnormals through `formatDouble`;
  every BMP character through `parseRadix` at radix 36; and every code point, 128 at a time,
  through `upper`, `urlEncode` and `base64`. All match. It found two problems, both fixed:
  Mojo's case tables predate Unicode 16 and map the Greek letters with ypogegrammeni to title
  case where Java spells them out with capital iota (90 code points, kept in `_upper_apart`),
  and EmberJson read an escaped surrogate pair on planes 2, 4, ... 16 as the plane below (the
  Java codec now writes whole pairs as the character).
- `gate` passes: 173 lines of Mojo for 41 of Java, the size limit exactly.
- `bench` (run twice, AMD Ryzen 9 3900X, 12 cores / 24 threads, load average 1.2-1.8): every
  function is slower through the bridge, 0.03x overall. The crossing alone is about 1 µs
  (`reverseBits`: 9-10 ns in Java, 1,030 ns through Mojo); `formatDouble`, which does exact
  big-number arithmetic, takes 12-13.5 µs against 80-91 ns; `parseRadix` comes closest, 0.21x
  (1.7 µs in Java, most cases throwing, against 7.8-8.0 µs).

files.README.md:
# psychrometrics-mojo

Three psychrometric routines of EnergyPlus version 27.1.0 (development, commit `7ab256b`,
`src/EnergyPlus/Psychrometrics.hh`) ported to Mojo with mojo-anything's C++ support: the
density of moist air (`PsyRhoAirFnPbTdbW`), its enthalpy (`PsyHFnTdbW`) and the dry-bulb
temperature from enthalpy (`PsyTdbFnHW`). Every recorded call is matched bit for bit, and the
unit passes `mojo-anything gate`.

## License

EnergyPlus is under its own BSD-style licence, kept in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) (EnergyPlus's
`LICENSE.txt`). The facade's statements are copied from EnergyPlus and the Mojo ports them, so
both carry that notice and those conditions, including clause (4) on the EnergyPlus name.

## What is here

- `facade/src/psychrometrics.{hpp,cpp}`: a free-function facade. In EnergyPlus the three
  routines are `constexpr` or `inline` in a header, so no object file defines them and
  mojo-anything refuses them (a shim in another file would have nothing to call). The facade
  defines them as plain functions in `EnergyPlus::Psychrometrics` with the statements copied
  unchanged; `Real64` and `Constant::Kelvin` are EnergyPlus's definitions, and the unqualified
  `max` is `std::max`, which for two doubles is what ObjexxFCL's `max` computes
  (`a < b ? b : a`). The rest of the header, which takes `EnergyPlusData &state`, is not here.
- `psychrometrics-mojo/`: the unit `bridge` made from the facade (`kind: c-abi`,
  `language: cpp`): `port.mojo` (the port), `exports.mojo` (the C symbols
  `cpp__EnergyPlus__Psychrometrics__<name>`), `cpp/shim.cpp` (those symbols over the facade, for
  recording) and `cpp/wrapper.cpp` (the facade's functions with their original signatures over
  the Mojo library, for C++ callers). Its manifest's `root` is `../facade`.

| Function | Cases | Match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `PsyRhoAirFnPbTdbW` | 3,226 | 3,226 |
| `PsyHFnTdbW` | 3,216 | 3,216 |
| `PsyTdbFnHW` | 3,216 | 3,216 |
| Total | 9,658 | 9,658 |

Recorded and replayed on 2026-11-22 on Linux x86-64 only (Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL, g++ 13.3 at `-O1`,
Mojo 1.2.0 with `--fp-mode contract=off`); recorded again with `-ffp-contract=off`, the cases are
byte for byte the same. Not run on other platforms or compilers. The
inputs are `scripts/inputs.py`'s 9,000 seeded calls over the ranges EnergyPlus sees (pressure
40 to 120 kPa, dry-bulb -60 to 70 C, humidity ratio 0 to 0.05, enthalpy -100 to 300 kJ/kg), the
1e-5 floor of the humidity ratio approached from both sides, and edge values (-0, absolute
zero, 1e300), plus mojo-anything's 658 generated cases and traps (subnormals, the largest
double, infinities).

## Found along the way

The first port, the statements written as they are in C++, matched 8,267 of 9,658 cases. The
1,391 misses were in all three functions (663 `PsyHFnTdbW`, 688 `PsyTdbFnHW`, 40
`PsyRhoAirFnPbTdbW`); 1,087 were one unit in the last place, and where a sum cancels (an
enthalpy near `2.50094e6 * W`) up to 730 units. `mojo build` fused `a * b + c` (as in
`1.00484e3 * TDB + w * (...)`) into one multiply-add with one rounding by default, where g++
13.3 at `-O1` for x86-64 rounds the product and the sum separately. mojo-anything now builds C
ABI units with `--fp-mode contract=off` and records the original with `-ffp-contract=off`, and
the port, the C++ statements as they are, matches every case with no multiply-add in its
library.
`max(dw, 1.0e-5)` is ported as `a < b ? b : a` rather than Mojo's `max`, so a NaN humidity ratio
stays NaN as it does in C++.

## Speed

`bench` runs (it times both libraries through the driver, each call crossing ctypes), but no
numbers are published yet: the machine these runs were made on was shared with other heavy
jobs. Numbers are pending a quiet machine.

## Reproduce

Needs a C++ compiler, Python 3, pixi, cargo and git; run on Linux x86-64 only. From the repository
root:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NREL/EnergyPlus.git /tmp/EnergyPlus   # for the facade check
EP=/tmp/EnergyPlus demo/real-world/psychrometrics-mojo/scripts/verify.sh
```

`verify.sh` checks each copied statement against `Psychrometrics.hh` when `EP` is set, then
records the facade, builds the Mojo library, replays every case and runs `gate`.

files.scripts/verify.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks the facade's statements against EnergyPlus's Psychrometrics.hh (when EP points at an
# EnergyPlus checkout), then records the facade on scripts/inputs.py's inputs and mojo-anything's
# generated cases, builds the Mojo port, replays every case and runs gate. Needs a C++ compiler,
# Python 3, pixi and cargo.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)
UNIT=$HERE/psychrometrics-mojo
MA=${MA:-$REPO/target/release/mojo-anything}
[ -x "$MA" ] || cargo build --release --manifest-path "$REPO/Cargo.toml"

if [ -n "${EP:-}" ]; then
  header=$EP/src/EnergyPlus/Psychrometrics.hh
  grep -E '^\s*(return|Real64 const W)' "$HERE/facade/src/psychrometrics.cpp" | while IFS= read -r line; do
    grep -qF -- "$(echo "$line" | sed 's/^ *//')" "$header" || { echo "not in $header: $line"; exit 1; }
  done
  echo "== the facade's statements are EnergyPlus's"
fi

python3 "$HERE/scripts/inputs.py" "$UNIT/inputs.jsonl"
echo "== psychrometrics-mojo"
"$MA" record "$UNIT" --inputs "$UNIT/inputs.jsonl" | grep Recorded | sed 's/ in .*//'
"$MA" build "$UNIT" > /dev/null
"$MA" diff "$UNIT" | sed -n 1p
"$MA" gate "$UNIT" | tail -1

files.README.md:
# psychrometrics-mojo

Three psychrometric routines of EnergyPlus version 27.1.0 (development, commit `7ab256b`,
`src/EnergyPlus/Psychrometrics.hh`) ported to Mojo with mojo-anything's C++ support: the
density of moist air (`PsyRhoAirFnPbTdbW`), its enthalpy (`PsyHFnTdbW`) and the dry-bulb
temperature from enthalpy (`PsyTdbFnHW`). Every recorded call is matched bit for bit, and the
unit passes `mojo-anything gate`.

## License

EnergyPlus is under its own BSD-style licence, kept in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) (EnergyPlus's
`LICENSE.txt`). The facade's statements are copied from EnergyPlus and the Mojo ports them, so
both carry that notice and those conditions, including clause (4) on the EnergyPlus name.

## What is here

- `facade/src/psychrometrics.{hpp,cpp}`: a free-function facade. In EnergyPlus the three
  routines are `constexpr` or `inline` in a header, so no object file defines them and
  mojo-anything refuses them (a shim in another file would have nothing to call). The facade
  defines them as plain functions in `EnergyPlus::Psychrometrics` with the statements copied
  unchanged; `Real64` and `Constant::Kelvin` are EnergyPlus's definitions, and the unqualified
  `max` is `std::max`, which for two doubles is what ObjexxFCL's `max` computes
  (`a < b ? b : a`). The rest of the header, which takes `EnergyPlusData &state`, is not here.
- `psychrometrics-mojo/`: the unit `bridge` made from the facade (`kind: c-abi`,
  `language: cpp`): `port.mojo` (the port), `exports.mojo` (the C symbols
  `cpp__EnergyPlus__Psychrometrics__<name>`), `cpp/shim.cpp` (those symbols over the facade, for
  recording) and `cpp/wrapper.cpp` (the facade's functions with their original signatures over
  the Mojo library, for C++ callers). Its manifest's `root` is `../facade`.

| Function | Cases | Match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `PsyRhoAirFnPbTdbW` | 3,226 | 3,226 |
| `PsyHFnTdbW` | 3,216 | 3,216 |
| `PsyTdbFnHW` | 3,216 | 3,216 |
| Total | 9,658 | 9,658 |

Recorded and replayed on 2026-11-22 on Linux x86-64 only (Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL, g++ 13.3 at `-O1`,
Mojo 1.2.0 with `--fp-mode contract=off`); recorded again with `-ffp-contract=off`, the cases are
byte for byte the same. Not run on other platforms or compilers. The
inputs are `scripts/inputs.py`'s 9,000 seeded calls over the ranges EnergyPlus sees (pressure
40 to 120 kPa, dry-bulb -60 to 70 C, humidity ratio 0 to 0.05, enthalpy -100 to 300 kJ/kg), the
1e-5 floor of the humidity ratio approached from both sides, and edge values (-0, absolute
zero, 1e300), plus mojo-anything's 658 generated cases and traps (subnormals, the largest
double, infinities).

## Found along the way

The first port, the statements written as they are in C++, matched 8,267 of 9,658 cases. The
1,391 misses were in all three functions (663 `PsyHFnTdbW`, 688 `PsyTdbFnHW`, 40
`PsyRhoAirFnPbTdbW`); 1,087 were one unit in the last place, and where a sum cancels (an
enthalpy near `2.50094e6 * W`) up to 730 units. `mojo build` fused `a * b + c` (as in
`1.00484e3 * TDB + w * (...)`) into one multiply-add with one rounding by default, where g++
13.3 at `-O1` for x86-64 rounds the product and the sum separately. mojo-anything now builds C
ABI units with `--fp-mode contract=off` and records the original with `-ffp-contract=off`, and
the port, the C++ statements as they are, matches every case with no multiply-add in its
library.
`max(dw, 1.0e-5)` is ported as `a < b ? b : a` rather than Mojo's `max`, so a NaN humidity ratio
stays NaN as it does in C++.

## Speed

`bench` runs (it times both libraries through the driver, each call crossing ctypes), but no
numbers are published yet: the machine these runs were made on was shared with other heavy
jobs. Numbers are pending a quiet machine.

## Reproduce

Needs a C++ compiler, Python 3, pixi, cargo and git; run on Linux x86-64 only. From the repository
root:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NREL/EnergyPlus.git /tmp/EnergyPlus   # for the facade check
EP=/tmp/EnergyPlus demo/real-world/psychrometrics-mojo/scripts/verify.sh
```

`verify.sh` checks each copied statement against `Psychrometrics.hh` when `EP` is set, then
records the facade, builds the Mojo library, replays every case and runs `gate`.

mojo-anything record .   # record what the original does

files.scripts/verify.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks the facade's statements against EnergyPlus's Psychrometrics.hh (when EP points at an
# EnergyPlus checkout), then records the facade on scripts/inputs.py's inputs and mojo-anything's
# generated cases, builds the Mojo port, replays every case and runs gate. Needs a C++ compiler,
# Python 3, pixi and cargo.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)
UNIT=$HERE/psychrometrics-mojo
MA=${MA:-$REPO/target/release/mojo-anything}
[ -x "$MA" ] || cargo build --release --manifest-path "$REPO/Cargo.toml"

if [ -n "${EP:-}" ]; then
  header=$EP/src/EnergyPlus/Psychrometrics.hh
  grep -E '^\s*(return|Real64 const W)' "$HERE/facade/src/psychrometrics.cpp" | while IFS= read -r line; do
    grep -qF -- "$(echo "$line" | sed 's/^ *//')" "$header" || { echo "not in $header: $line"; exit 1; }
  done
  echo "== the facade's statements are EnergyPlus's"
fi

python3 "$HERE/scripts/inputs.py" "$UNIT/inputs.jsonl"
echo "== psychrometrics-mojo"
"$MA" record "$UNIT" --inputs "$UNIT/inputs.jsonl" | grep Recorded | sed 's/ in .*//'
"$MA" build "$UNIT" > /dev/null
"$MA" diff "$UNIT" | sed -n 1p
"$MA" gate "$UNIT" | tail -1

# mojo-anything; regenerate with `mojo-anything refresh`.

require "fiddle"
require "json"
require "rbconfig"

module MojoAnythingCodec
  module_function

  def enc(v)
    case v
    when Float
      return { "$num" => "NaN" } if v.nan?
      return { "$num" => v.positive? ? "Infinity" : "-Infinity" } if v.infinite?
      return { "$num" => "-0" } if v.zero? && (1.0 / v).negative?

      v
    when Integer, String, true, false, nil then v
    when Symbol then { "$sym" => v.to_s }
    when Array then v.map { |x| enc(x) }
    when Hash
      if v.keys.all? { |k| k.is_a?(String) }
        v.transform_values { |x| enc(x) }
      else
        { "$hash" => v.map { |k, x| [enc(k), enc(x)] } }
      end
    else
      { "$object" => v.class.name, "value" => v.respond_to?(:to_h) ? enc(v.to_h) : v.inspect }
    end
  end

  def dec(v)
    case v
    when Array then v.map { |x| dec(x) }
    when Hash
      if v.size == 1 && v.key?("$num")

        v["$sym"].to_sym
      elsif v.size == 1 && v.key?("$hash")

A small CLI used to test `mojo-anything app record` and `app replay`.

```console

HELLO WORLD
$ tcli len héllo
$ tcli div 7 2
7 / 2 = 3 remainder 1
$ echo "one two three" | tcli words
3
$ tcli copy input.txt out.txt
$ tcli now
$ tcli nope
```

<?php

function usage(): int
{
    fwrite(STDERR, "usage: tcli upper|len|div|words|copy|now\n");
    return 1;
}

function run(array $argv): int
{
    if (count($argv) === 0) {
        return usage();
    }
    $cmd = array_shift($argv);

  warn "usage: tcli upper|len|div|words|copy|now"
  1
end

def run(argv)
  return usage if argv.empty?

  cmd, *args = argv.map { |a| a.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8") }
  if cmd == "upper"
    puts args.join(" ").upcase
  elsif cmd == "len" && args.size == 1
    puts args[0].length
  elsif cmd == "div" && args.size == 2
    unless args.all? { |a| a.b.match?(/\A-?\d+\z/) }
      warn "error: not a number"
      return 2
    end
    a, b = args.map(&:to_i)
    if b.zero?
      warn "error: division by zero"
      return 2
    end
    puts "#{a} / #{b} = #{a / b} remainder #{a % b}"
  elsif cmd == "words"
    puts $stdin.read.b.split.size
  elsif cmd == "copy" && args.size == 2
    begin
      text = File.read(args[0], encoding: "UTF-8")
    rescue SystemCallError
      warn "error: cannot read #{args[0]}"
      return 1
    end
    begin
      File.write(args[1], text.upcase)
    rescue SystemCallError
      warn "error: cannot write #{args[1]}"
      return 1
    end
    puts "copied #{text.length} characters"
  elsif cmd == "now"
    puts "now: #{Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_REALTIME, :nanosecond)}"
  else
    return usage
  end
  0
end

exit run(ARGV)

<?php

function usage(): int
{
    fwrite(STDERR, "usage: tcli upper|len|div|words|copy|now\n");
    return 1;
}

function run(array $argv): int
{
    if (count($argv) === 0) {
        return usage();
    }
    $cmd = array_shift($argv);
    $args = $argv;
    if ($cmd === 'upper') {
        echo mb_strtoupper(implode(' ', $args), 'UTF-8'), "\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'len' && count($args) === 1) {
        echo mb_strlen($args[0], 'UTF-8'), "\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'div' && count($args) === 2) {
        foreach ($args as $a) {
            if (!preg_match('/\A-?\d+\z/', $a)) {
                fwrite(STDERR, "error: not a number\n");
                return 2;
            }
        }
        [$a, $b] = array_map('intval', $args);
        if ($b === 0) {
            fwrite(STDERR, "error: division by zero\n");
            return 2;
        }
        echo "$a / $b = ", intdiv($a, $b), " remainder ", $a % $b, "\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'words') {
        $text = trim(stream_get_contents(STDIN), " \t\n\r\v\f");
        echo $text === '' ? 0 : count(preg_split('/[ \t\n\r\v\f]+/', $text)), "\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'copy' && count($args) === 2) {
        $text = $args[0] === '' ? false : @file_get_contents($args[0]);
        if ($text === false) {
            fwrite(STDERR, "error: cannot read {$args[0]}\n");
            return 1;
        }
        if ($args[1] === '' || @file_put_contents($args[1], mb_strtoupper($text, 'UTF-8')) === false) {
            fwrite(STDERR, "error: cannot write {$args[1]}\n");
            return 1;
        }
        echo 'copied ', mb_strlen($text, 'UTF-8'), " characters\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'now') {
        echo 'now: ', hrtime(true), "\n";
    } else {
        return usage();
    }
    return 0;
}

exit(run(array_slice($argv, 1)));

    respond(200, TEXT, mb_strtoupper($body, 'UTF-8'));

    [$a, $b] = [rawurldecode($parts[1]), rawurldecode($parts[2])];

        respond(400, TEXT, "error: not a number\n");

        respond(400, TEXT, "error: division by zero\n");

require "socket"

TEXT = "text/plain; charset=utf-8"
REASONS = { 200 => "OK", 400 => "Bad Request", 404 => "Not Found" }.freeze

def respond(client, status, type, body)
  body = body.b
  client.write("HTTP/1.1 #{status} #{REASONS[status]}\r\nContent-Type: #{type}\r\n" \
               "Content-Length: #{body.bytesize}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
  client.write(body)
end

def unquote(text)
  text.b.gsub(/%([0-9A-Fa-f]{2})/) { Regexp.last_match(1).hex.chr }.force_encoding("UTF-8")
end

def route(method, path, body)
  parts = path.split("/", -1)[1..] || []
  if method == "GET" && path == "/hello"
    [200, "application/json", '{"message":"hello"}']
  elsif method == "POST" && path == "/upper"
    [200, TEXT, body.scrub.upcase]
  elsif method == "GET" && parts.size == 3 && parts[0] == "div"
    a, b = parts[1..].map { |p| unquote(p) }
    return [400, TEXT, "error: not a number\n"] unless [a, b].all? { |x| x.b.match?(/\A-?\d+\z/) }

    a, b = a.to_i, b.to_i
    return [400, TEXT, "error: division by zero\n"] if b.zero?

    [200, TEXT, "#{a} / #{b} = #{a / b} remainder #{a % b}\n"]
  elsif method == "GET" && path == "/now"
    [200, TEXT, "now: #{Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_REALTIME, :nanosecond)}\n"]
  else
    [404, TEXT, "not found\n"]
  end
end

server = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", Integer(ENV.fetch("PORT", "8080")))
loop do
  client = server.accept
  begin
    request_line = client.gets
    next unless request_line

    method, target = request_line.split(" ")
    headers = {}
    while (line = client.gets) && line != "\r\n"
      key, val = line.split(":", 2)
      headers[key.strip.downcase] = val.to_s.strip
    end
    body = client.read(headers.fetch("content-length", "0").to_i).to_s.force_encoding("UTF-8")
    respond(client, *route(method, target.split("?", 2)[0], body))
  ensure
    client.close
  end
end

require "socket"

TEXT = "text/plain; charset=utf-8"
REASONS = { 200 => "OK", 400 => "Bad Request", 404 => "Not Found" }.freeze

def respond(client, status, type, body)
  body = body.b
  client.write("HTTP/1.1 #{status} #{REASONS[status]}\r\nContent-Type: #{type}\r\n" \
               "Content-Length: #{body.bytesize}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
  client.write(body)
end

def unquote(text)
  text.b.gsub(/%([0-9A-Fa-f]{2})/) { Regexp.last_match(1).hex.chr }.force_encoding("UTF-8")
end

def route(method, path, body)
  parts = path.split("/", -1)[1..] || []
  if method == "GET" && path == "/hello"
    [200, "application/json", '{"message":"hello"}']
  elsif method == "POST" && path == "/upper"
    [200, TEXT, body.scrub.upcase]
  elsif method == "GET" && parts.size == 3 && parts[0] == "div"
    a, b = parts[1..].map { |p| unquote(p) }
    return [400, TEXT, "error: not a number\n"] unless [a, b].all? { |x| x.b.match?(/\A-?\d+\z/) }

    a, b = a.to_i, b.to_i
    return [400, TEXT, "error: division by zero\n"] if b.zero?

    [200, TEXT, "#{a} / #{b} = #{a / b} remainder #{a % b}\n"]
  elsif method == "GET" && path == "/now"
    [200, TEXT, "now: #{Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_REALTIME, :nanosecond)}\n"]
  else
    [404, TEXT, "not found\n"]
  end
end

server = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", Integer(ENV.fetch("PORT", "8080")))
loop do
  client = server.accept
  begin
    request_line = client.gets
    next unless request_line

    method, target = request_line.split(" ")
    headers = {}
    while (line = client.gets) && line != "\r\n"
      key, val = line.split(":", 2)
      headers[key.strip.downcase] = val.to_s.strip
    end
    body = client.read(headers.fetch("content-length", "0").to_i).to_s.force_encoding("UTF-8")
    respond(client, *route(method, target.split("?", 2)[0], body))
  ensure
    client.close
  end
end

const TEXT = 'text/plain; charset=utf-8';

function respond(int $status, string $type, string $body): void
{
    header_remove('X-Powered-By');
    http_response_code($status);
    header("Content-Type: $type");
    echo $body;
}

$method = $_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'];
$path = parse_url($_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'], PHP_URL_PATH);
$parts = array_slice(explode('/', $path), 1);

if ($method === 'GET' && $path === '/hello') {
    respond(200, 'application/json', '{"message":"hello"}');
} elseif ($method === 'POST' && $path === '/upper') {
    $body = mb_scrub(file_get_contents('php://input'), 'UTF-8');
    respond(200, TEXT, mb_strtoupper($body, 'UTF-8'));
} elseif ($method === 'GET' && count($parts) === 3 && $parts[0] === 'div') {
    [$a, $b] = [rawurldecode($parts[1]), rawurldecode($parts[2])];
    if (!preg_match('/\A-?\d+\z/', $a) || !preg_match('/\A-?\d+\z/', $b)) {
        respond(400, TEXT, "error: not a number\n");
    } elseif ((int) $b === 0) {
        respond(400, TEXT, "error: division by zero\n");
    } else {
        [$a, $b] = [(int) $a, (int) $b];
        respond(200, TEXT, "$a / $b = " . intdiv($a, $b) . " remainder " . ($a % $b) . "\n");
    }
} elseif ($method === 'GET' && $path === '/now') {
    respond(200, TEXT, 'now: ' . hrtime(true) . "\n");
} else {
    respond(404, TEXT, "not found\n");
}

require "socket"

TEXT = "text/plain; charset=utf-8"
REASONS = { 200 => "OK", 400 => "Bad Request", 404 => "Not Found" }.freeze

def respond(client, status, type, body)
  body = body.b
  client.write("HTTP/1.1 #{status} #{REASONS[status]}\r\nContent-Type: #{type}\r\n" \
               "Content-Length: #{body.bytesize}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
  client.write(body)
end

def unquote(text)
  text.b.gsub(/%([0-9A-Fa-f]{2})/) { Regexp.last_match(1).hex.chr }.force_encoding("UTF-8")
end

def route(method, path, body)
  parts = path.split("/", -1)[1..] || []
  if method == "GET" && path == "/hello"
    [200, "application/json", '{"message":"hello"}']
  elsif method == "POST" && path == "/upper"
    [200, TEXT, body.scrub.upcase]
  elsif method == "GET" && parts.size == 3 && parts[0] == "div"
    a, b = parts[1..].map { |p| unquote(p) }
    return [400, TEXT, "error: not a number\n"] unless [a, b].all? { |x| x.b.match?(/\A-?\d+\z/) }

    a, b = a.to_i, b.to_i
    return [400, TEXT, "error: division by zero\n"] if b.zero?

    [200, TEXT, "#{a} / #{b} = #{a / b} remainder #{a % b}\n"]
  elsif method == "GET" && path == "/now"
    [200, TEXT, "now: #{Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_REALTIME, :nanosecond)}\n"]
  else
    [404, TEXT, "not found\n"]
  end
end

server = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", Integer(ENV.fetch("PORT", "8080")))
loop do
  client = server.accept
  begin
    request_line = client.gets
    next unless request_line

    method, target = request_line.split(" ")
    headers = {}
    while (line = client.gets) && line != "\r\n"
      key, val = line.split(":", 2)
      headers[key.strip.downcase] = val.to_s.strip
    end
    body = client.read(headers.fetch("content-length", "0").to_i).to_s.force_encoding("UTF-8")
    respond(client, *route(method, target.split("?", 2)[0], body))
  ensure
    client.close
  end
end

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Acme\Textkit\Text;

use Acme\Textkit\Util\Ascii;

final class Slug
{
    /**
     * @param string $text
     * @return string
     */
    public static function slugify(string $text, string $sep = '-'): string
    {
        $ascii = Ascii::fold($text);
        $slug = preg_replace('/[^a-z0-9]+/', $sep, strtolower($ascii));
        return trim($slug, $sep);
    }

    public static function truncate(string $text, int $max): string
    {
        if ($max < 0) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException('max must not be negative');
        }
        return mb_substr($text, 0, $max);
    }
}

    # @param total [Integer]
    # @param per_page [Integer]

      raise ArgumentError, "per_page must be positive" unless per_page.positive?

    def mean(values)

module Textkit
  # Word helpers.
  module Words
    # Lowercases text and joins its words with sep.
    # @param text [String]
    # @param sep [String]
    # @param max [Integer, nil] cut the slug to this many characters
    # @return [String]
    def self.slugify(text, sep = "-", max: nil)
      slug = text.downcase.scan(/[[:alnum:]]+/).join(sep)
      max ? slug[0, max].chomp(sep) : slug
    end

    # @param text [String]
    # @return [Hash{String => Integer}]
    def self.word_count(text)
      text.split.map(&:downcase).tally
    end

    # @param text [String]
    # @return [String]
    def self.titleize(text)
      text.split(/(\s+)/).map(&:capitalize).join
    end

    def self.each_word(text)
      text.split.each { |w| yield w }
    end
  end
end

files.tcli.php:
<?php

function usage(): int
{
    fwrite(STDERR, "usage: tcli upper|len|div|words|copy|now\n");
    return 1;
}

function run(array $argv): int
{
    if (count($argv) === 0) {
        return usage();
    }
    $cmd = array_shift($argv);
    $args = $argv;
    if ($cmd === 'upper') {
        echo mb_strtoupper(implode(' ', $args), 'UTF-8'), "\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'len' && count($args) === 1) {
        echo mb_strlen($args[0], 'UTF-8'), "\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'div' && count($args) === 2) {
        foreach ($args as $a) {
            if (!preg_match('/\A-?\d+\z/', $a)) {
                fwrite(STDERR, "error: not a number\n");
                return 2;
            }
        }
        [$a, $b] = array_map('intval', $args);
        if ($b === 0) {
            fwrite(STDERR, "error: division by zero\n");
            return 2;
        }
        echo "$a / $b = ", intdiv($a, $b), " remainder ", $a % $b, "\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'words') {
        $text = trim(stream_get_contents(STDIN), " \t\n\r\v\f");
        echo $text === '' ? 0 : count(preg_split('/[ \t\n\r\v\f]+/', $text)), "\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'copy' && count($args) === 2) {
        $text = $args[0] === '' ? false : @file_get_contents($args[0]);
        if ($text === false) {
            fwrite(STDERR, "error: cannot read {$args[0]}\n");
            return 1;
        }
        if ($args[1] === '' || @file_put_contents($args[1], mb_strtoupper($text, 'UTF-8')) === false) {
            fwrite(STDERR, "error: cannot write {$args[1]}\n");
            return 1;
        }
        echo 'copied ', mb_strlen($text, 'UTF-8'), " characters\n";
    } elseif ($cmd === 'now') {
        echo 'now: ', hrtime(true), "\n";
    } else {
        return usage();
    }
    return 0;
}

exit(run(array_slice($argv, 1)));

files.tcli.rb:
def usage
  warn "usage: tcli upper|len|div|words|copy|now"
  1
end

def run(argv)
  return usage if argv.empty?

  cmd, *args = argv.map { |a| a.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8") }
  if cmd == "upper"
    puts args.join(" ").upcase
  elsif cmd == "len" && args.size == 1
    puts args[0].length
  elsif cmd == "div" && args.size == 2
    unless args.all? { |a| a.b.match?(/\A-?\d+\z/) }
      warn "error: not a number"
      return 2
    end
    a, b = args.map(&:to_i)
    if b.zero?
      warn "error: division by zero"
      return 2
    end
    puts "#{a} / #{b} = #{a / b} remainder #{a % b}"
  elsif cmd == "words"
    puts $stdin.read.b.split.size
  elsif cmd == "copy" && args.size == 2
    begin
      text = File.read(args[0], encoding: "UTF-8")
    rescue SystemCallError
      warn "error: cannot read #{args[0]}"
      return 1
    end
    begin
      File.write(args[1], text.upcase)
    rescue SystemCallError
      warn "error: cannot write #{args[1]}"
      return 1
    end
    puts "copied #{text.length} characters"
  elsif cmd == "now"
    puts "now: #{Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_REALTIME, :nanosecond)}"
  else
    return usage
  end
  0
end

exit run(ARGV)

# frozen_string_literal: true

# A fixture for Ruby units ported to Mojo (`tests/ruby_mojo.rs`).
module Textkit
  # Repeats s n times; n must be 0 to 8.
  #
  # @param s [String]
  # @param n [Integer]
  # @return [String]
  def self.repeat(s, n)
    raise ArgumentError, "bad count" if n.negative? || n > 8

    s * n
  end

  # Returns v as it is: symbols, hashes with any keys, arrays.
  #
  # @param v [Object]
  # @return [Object]
  def self.echo(v)
    v
  end

  # Half of x.
  #
  # @param x [Float]
  # @return [Float]
  def self.half(x)
    x / 2.0
  end
end

```

# tcli

A small CLI used to test `mojo-anything app record` and `app replay`.

```console
$ tcli upper hello world
HELLO WORLD
$ tcli len héllo
$ tcli div 7 2
7 / 2 = 3 remainder 1
$ echo "one two three" | tcli words
3
$ tcli copy input.txt out.txt
$ tcli now
$ tcli nope
```
